The company has previously said it believes it's well positioned to weather macroeconomic pressures. Company executives will hold a conference call with analysts at 8 a.m. ET. In this article WMT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers enter a Walmart store in Charlotte, North Carolina, Aug. 30, 2026. Travis Dove | Bloomberg | Getty Images Walmart is scheduled to report its third fiscal quarter earnings Thursday as the retailer prepares for the holiday season with an increased emphasis on value amid lower consumer sentiment. The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership. Here's what the company is expected to report for its fiscal third quarter, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 64 cents expected Revenue: $187.27 billion expected Walmart previously said it expects third-quarter net sales to climb 3% to 3.75%. CFO John David Rainey told CNBC last quarter that Walmart's "business is strong" and that he's encouraged by its progress. The company is typically well insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef. It also saw a significant boost from tariff refunds, which Rainey said Walmart would use to cut prices. In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with its club subsidiary, Sam's Club, as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships. The retailer is also rolling out technology in its stores to improve the customer experience, including light-up digital shelf labels that are connected to its app. Those shelf labels and Walmart's AI push have also sparked concerns that the retailer could try to change prices based on demand and shoppers' personal data, which Walmart has denied. Analysts from UBS wrote in a note last week that they believe the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results will show healthy market share gains. "E-commerce continues to scale, the company's higher-margin alternative revenue streams continue to grow and Walmart is increasingly able to fund investments in price and convenience while still producing attractive operating income growth," the analysts wrote. They added that they expect Walmart's fourth-quarter outlook to include "robust operating income growth." Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date.
